title: The Structure Theorem Behind λ(2ᵏ)
content: For an odd prime power pᵏ the unit group (ℤ/pᵏℤ)ˣ is cyclic, but powers of two are exceptional: for k ≥ 3 the group (ℤ/2ᵏℤ)ˣ has no primitive root. The classical structure theorem (Gauss; Ireland & Rosen Ch. 4) says it is instead a direct product of two cyclic groups — ℤ/2 generated by −1, and ℤ/2ᵏ⁻² generated by 5 — so (ℤ/2ᵏℤ)ˣ ≅ ℤ/2 × ℤ/2ᵏ⁻². The parent records only the value λ(2ᵏ) = 2ᵏ⁻² from Mathlib; this entry proves the underlying decomposition that EXPLAINS it. Mathlib knows the group is non-cyclic and that 5 has order 2ᵏ⁻², but does not package the explicit two-generator product — the one missing step being −1 ∉ ⟨5⟩.

title: The Two Generators and the Reduction Homomorphism
content: Section I sets up the explicit generators. five is the unit 5 ∈ (ℤ/2ⁿ⁺³ℤ)ˣ; orderOf_five transports Mathlib's ZMod.orderOf_five to the unit group to get orderOf 5 = 2ⁿ⁺¹. The reduction homomorphism red : (ℤ/2ⁿ⁺³ℤ)ˣ → (ℤ/4ℤ)ˣ is built from ZMod.castHom (using 4 ∣ 2ⁿ⁺³) lifted via Units.map; red_five computes red 5 = 1 (since 5 ≡ 1 mod 4) and red_neg_one gives red (−1) = −1. orderOf_neg_one proves orderOf (−1) = 2 via orderOf_eq_prime — using red to rule out (−1) = 1. The parametrization k = n + 3 keeps every exponent (2ᵏ⁻¹, 2ᵏ⁻², 2ᵏ) a genuine power, avoiding truncated natural subtraction.
mathContext: $5$ has order $2^{n+1} = 2^{k-2}$; $-1$ has order $2$. Reduction mod 4: $5 \mapsto 1$, $-1 \mapsto -1$ in $(\mathbb{Z}/4\mathbb{Z})^\times = \{\pm 1\}$.

title: The Crux: −1 ∉ ⟨5⟩
content: neg_one_notMem_zpowers_five is the mathematical heart and the one step genuinely absent from Mathlib. It proves −1 is never a power of 5 by reduction mod 4: if 5^m = −1, applying the homomorphism red sends the left side to red(5)^m = 1^m = 1 and the right side to −1, forcing 1 = −1 in (ℤ/4ℤ)ˣ — refuted by kernel decide. This is precisely the obstruction to (ℤ/2ᵏℤ)ˣ being cyclic: the two cyclic factors are independent because −1 escapes ⟨5⟩. disjoint_neg_one_five then derives ⟨−1⟩ ∩ ⟨5⟩ = {1} by a parity split: (−1)^m is 1 for even m, and for odd m equals −1, which would land −1 ∈ ⟨5⟩, contradicting the crux.
mathContext: Powers of 5 stay $\equiv 1 \pmod 4$ while $-1 \equiv 3$; the homomorphism $\mathrm{red}$ kills 5 but not $-1$, so $5^m = -1$ is impossible. Hence $\langle -1\rangle \cap \langle 5\rangle = \{1\}$.

title: The Internal Direct Product and Carmichael Recovery
content: Section III assembles the theorem. card_units computes |(ℤ/2ⁿ⁺³ℤ)ˣ| = φ(2ⁿ⁺³) = 2ⁿ⁺². isComplement'_neg_one_five then feeds the disjointness (the crux) and the order count |⟨−1⟩|·|⟨5⟩| = 2·2ⁿ⁺¹ = 2ⁿ⁺² = |G| to isComplement'_of_card_mul_and_disjoint, yielding the internal direct product (ℤ/2ᵏℤ)ˣ = ⟨−1⟩ × ⟨5⟩ — so every unit is uniquely (−1)ᵃ·5ᵇ. Finally carmichael_two_pow recovers the parent's λ(2ᵏ) = 2ᵏ⁻² as the exponent of the product (lcm of the factor orders), delegating the arithmetic to Mathlib's carmichael_two_pow_of_ne_two.
